papers.title: Dynamic Chemical Changes of Ti3C2Tx MXenes in Halide Perovskite Precursor Environments
papers.abstract: The integration of two-dimensional Ti3C2Tx MXenes into Halide Perovskite (HaP) optoelectronics has shown immense potential for enhancing device performance, yet the fundamental chemical interactions within the precursor ink (a critical stage determining the final material state) remain largely unexplored. This study presents a comprehensive investigation into the chemical stability and surface evolution of Ti3C2Tx MXenes when exposed to the individual and combined components of a model methylammonium lead iodide (MAPbI3) solution. By combining detailed X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy (XPS) analysis with Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations, we decouple the complex interactions between MXenes and the ink constituents. We demonstrate that elemental iodine (I2) and polyiodides (In-) act as aggressive oxidizers, triggering rapid degradation and dissolution of the MXene flakes. Conversely, lead iodide (PbI2) induces a slower oxidation process driven by the strong adsorption of Pb2+ ions onto oxygen terminated sites. In stark contrast, methylammonium iodide (MAI) exhibits a stabilizing effect: it adsorbs onto the MXene surface via hydrogen bonding, effectively passivating the flakes and retarding degradation. In addition, our results reveal that the sequence of precursor addition governs the MXene surface state, requiring extra caution, but also enabling further tunability. These findings provide a critical view on how MXene integration with materials, in general, and HaP in particular, should be perceived, providing a fundamental for their rational engineering.

papers.title: Nonlocal Josephson coupling and current redistribution in a large-area graphene multiterminal Josephson junction
papers.abstract: Multiterminal Josephson junctions (MTJJs) extend conventional two-terminal Josephson physics to devices defined by multiple superconducting phases, where rich phenomena have been predicted. However, in conventional MTJJs, superconducting transport is often dominated by local coupling between neighboring leads, obscuring physics that goes beyond simple connectivity. Here, we realize a multiterminal Josephson network in a graphene Hall bar geometry with micron-scale dimensions, enabling substantial nonlocal coupling between distant terminals. Our key observation is a pronounced negative differential longitudinal resistance (NDLR) in the four-probe response near switching currents, while no such feature appears in two-terminal measurements. We reproduce the NDLR response with a network containing the interplay between two distinct forms of nonlocality: nonlocal Josephson coupling, which determines the switching sequence of the superconducting network, and nonlocal normal-state conductance, which redistributes current after different regions switch. Our results highlight the potential of the emergent NDLR for characterizing superconductor--semiconductor hybrid systems and for nonlinear circuits. Further, this Josephson Hall bar geometry provides a platform for exploring the interplay between mesoscopic superconductivity and many-body ground states in graphene-based heterostructures.

papers.title: Corrugated Niobene: Stability, Mechanical and Electronic Properties from First-Principles Calculations
papers.abstract: The growing diversity of two-dimensional (2D) materials has expanded opportunities in electronics, energy technologies, catalysis, and optical applications. Within this landscape, understanding how corrugated architectures accommodate metallic bonding and influence the stability and properties of monoelemental niobium sheets remains an open research direction. Here, we propose a corrugated niobene nanosheet, denoted c-Nb, and investigate its structural, energetic, vibrational, mechanical, electronic, and optical properties using density functional theory simulations. The optimized structure adopts a centrosymmetric P-3m1 symmetry, with six atoms per primitive cell and a geometrical thickness of 4.279 Angstrom. Its cohesive energy of -6.03 eV/atom indicates strong binding relative to isolated atoms, although bulk BCC Nb remains energetically favored by 2.49 eV/atom. The absence of imaginary phonon frequencies along the investigated high-symmetry path and the positive-definite in-plane stiffness matrix support dynamical and mechanical structural stability. Despite its pronounced corrugation, the nanosheet exhibits isotropic in-plane elasticity, with Young's and shear moduli of 43.66 N/m and 13.66 N/m, respectively, and a Poisson's ratio of 0.598. Electronic states near the Fermi level are dominated by Nb 4d orbitals, establishing multiband metallicity. These findings identify a corrugated structural candidate that combines strong cohesion, elastic compliance, and metallic electronic behavior, extending the structural diversity of monoelemental 2D metals and providing a basis for further exploration of niobium nanosheets in electronic and ultraviolet-responsive systems.

papers.title: The quantum geometry of the chemical bond
papers.abstract: Electronic properties of materials depend both on band energies and quantum geometry of electronic states. We relate bonding indices to the quantum geometric tensor (QGT), showing how chemical bonding dictates the momentum-space texture of bands, bridging chemical and physical descriptions of solids. We show the QGT decomposed into the three center bond index, weighted by their oriented area. Resolving these contributions by orbital pair reveals the donor--acceptor character that distinguish ionic, covalent, hypervalent, and metavalent bonding. We identify the bonding pattern for topology in materials: noncollinear three center bonds, which are the source of Berry curvature in solids. Bond fluctuation can be directly linked to electromagnetic response by resolving their energy spectrum, opening a quantitative route towards the design of physical properties of materials from bonding motifs.

papers.title: Homogeneous to multi-scale inhomogeneous complex magnetism in Ba3LnRu2O9 (Ln = Gd, Ho), Revealed by muSR and Machine-Learned Muon-Site Calculations
papers.abstract: We report a comprehensive muon spin rotation and relaxation (muSR) study of the hexagonal 6H-perovskites Ba3LnRu2O9 (Ln = Gd, Ho) to investigate the role of rare-earth anisotropy in the magnetic ground state of 4d-4f coupled systems. Ba3HoRu2O9 exhibits two successive magnetic orderings at TN1 = 46 K and TN2 = 10 K, leading to a complex magnetic ground state, whereas Ba3GdRu2O9, with Gd3+ (L = 0) S-state ions, shows primarily single magnetic ordering at TN = 14.5 K. Zero-field (ZF) and longitudinal-field (LF) muSR measurements reveal markedly different magnetic behavior despite their structural similarity. Ba3HoRu2O9 displays a multi-scale inhomogeneous magnetic state characterized by two-component exponential relaxation, broad local-field distributions, incomplete LF decoupling, and persistent spin dynamics. The muSR results identify two characteristic magnetic energy scales near 46 and 10 K, associated with correlated Ru-Ho interactions and quasistatic magnetic ordering, respectively. Redfield analysis further demonstrates strong local magnetic fields and distributed spin fluctuation timescales, confirming magnetic inhomogeneity. Machine-learning-assisted muon-site and dipolar-field calculations show that the broad field distribution naturally arises from muons sensing distinct coexisting magnetic domains at different structural sites. In contrast, Ba3GdRu2O9 exhibits a comparatively homogeneous antiferromagnetic ground state below 14.5 K, with Gaussian relaxation consistent with a narrow static field distribution. These results establish that the rare-earth ion in Ba3LnRu2O9 is a powerful tuning parameter, driving the ground state from homogeneous to complex, multi-scale inhomogeneous behavior through competing 4d-4f magnetic interactions.

papers.title: Electron binding by charge disorder surrounding gapped bilayer graphene
papers.abstract: Bilayer graphene (BLG) is a unique electronic material offering electrostatic tunability of its band gap. Here, we study how charge disorder in the dielectric environment modifies band-edge states by binding electrons and holes to Coulomb centres, taking into account the in- and out-of-plane dielectric response of Bernal bilayers. We apply this framework to (a) hBN-encapsulated medium-size-gap BLG used for gate-defined quantum dots, and (b) BLG under double n/p ionic gating. In hBN/BLG/hBN, we find that single remote charges produce only weakly bound states, with binding energies generally small compared with the BLG gap. Under ionic gating, we find that the bound states are too large to be trapped by individual ions -- localisation arises from fluctuations in the ion density, whose magnitude is limited by Coulomb charging energy at the freezing temperature $T_f$ of the ionic configuration. Thus, in both regimes, charge disorder does not produce deep midgap states, with the bound states remaining closer to the conduction and valence band edges.

papers.title: Improving the lower bound on the Laughlin gap: An SDP search
papers.abstract: A recent preprint by OpenAI resolved the spherical fermionic Laughlin spectral-gap conjecture for the full $V_1$ interaction by a Fock-space inequality: $H_Q^2\ge γH_Q$ on the lowest-Landau-level Fock space for all large flux $Q$ and every $γ$ below $0.0461673\ldots$, so that the gap above the Laughlin state at filling $1/3$ is at least $1/25$. That proof, with its original constant, has also been formalized in Lean. We show that the same argument supports a much larger constant. Two sharper estimates, a product-twirl bound for the three-body tail and a staircase price for the four-body allowance, raise the constant above $0.0601$ without changing the original certificate. Treating the auxiliary operators as the variables of a semidefinite program (SDP) and enlarging the finite set of orbital modes on which they act then gives $H_Q^2\geγH_Q$ for every $γ<γ_*=0.2190037845063196\ldots$, certified by exact rational arithmetic. Consequently the gap above the Laughlin state is at least $1/5$ for all sufficiently large spheres, and the untruncated planar $V_1$ Hamiltonian has positive spectrum bounded below by $γ_*$, uniformly in particle number and angular momentum. A heuristic extrapolation of the SDP optima suggests that auxiliary operators of the present form can give at most about $0.222$, while exact diagonalization of finite systems places the true gap near $0.4$. A larger family of auxiliary operators could push the bound further towards the true gap, and the SDP formulation makes such families easy to test. The proof of the improvement and the SDP search were completed by the AI model Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic) under the author's direction.

papers.title: Spectral optimization of spherical lattices and applications to classical and quantum interacting spin systems
papers.abstract: We develop an optimization algorithm for spherical lattice discretizations based on the spectrum of the discretized Laplace operator. Starting from refined icosahedral lattices, we minimize the splitting of the $(2\ell+1)$, $\ell=0,1,2,\dots$, continuum multiplets expected from $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ symmetry via gradient descent. This approach simultaneously produces lattices based on triangles with nearly uniform circumradii and perimeters. Although the optimization uses only the free-particle spectrum, we show that the resulting lattices carry over to interacting models. On the optimized lattices, rotational symmetry is restored for the critical Ising and Potts models and primary scaling dimensions are accurately reproduced for the three-dimensional Ising conformal field theory, when appropriate geometry-dependent interaction strengths are used. Higher-angular-momentum descendant states reveal weak residual symmetry breaking beyond the sectors protected by the underlying icosahedral symmetry.

papers.title: Entropy Production in Mesoscopic Electronic Transport Beyond Weak-Coupling
papers.abstract: We investigate the full statistics of entropy production in coherent mesoscopic conductors beyond the weak-coupling regime. Using the inside-outside perspective and the Landauer-Büttiker scattering framework, we relate entropy production to the full counting statistics of particle transport and show that the corresponding cumulant-generating function satisfies the fluctuation symmetry independently of the coupling strength. We obtain closed analytical expressions for the cumulant-generating function in the weak- and strong-coupling limits, enabling a detailed characterization of entropy production distributions and higher-order cumulants. These cumulants reveal distinct signatures of resonant transport and coherent fermionic partitioning. While coupling-induced broadening substantially modifies the transport statistics, the fluctuation symmetry imposed by microscopic reversibility remains preserved in the long-time limit.

papers.title: Search for free non-Abelian anyons in paired composite-fermion states
papers.abstract: The even-denominator fractional quantum Hall (FQH) states, understood as topological superconductors of composite fermions, are predicted to support elementary quasiparticles (QPs) or quasiholes (QHs) obeying non-Abelian braid statistics. Using the microscopic framework of parton theory, we investigate many experimentally observed paired composite-fermion states and find that their elementary QPs and QHs in general bind to form Abelian molecules, thus obscuring non-Abelian braid statistics. An exception is the $ν=1/2$ state in wide quantum wells, where our calculations show free QPs or QHs; we thus identify this state as an especially promising candidate for realizing and studying non-Abelian braid statistics. We also indicate how the study of such bound states can help reveal the topological structure of the state.

papers.title: Entropic-ordered superfluid
papers.abstract: We present a minimal classical lattice model of superfluidity at arbitrarily high temperatures, using a modified three-dimensional XY model with ``soft" rotors. The global U(1) symmetry is spontaneously broken above a positive critical temperature due to entropic order. We study hydrodynamics in this high-temperature regime and verify consistency with the fluctuation-dissipation theorem, explaining how the large noise variance at very high temperatures is not sufficient to destroy superfluidity or the long lifetime of Goldstone modes.

papers.title: Odd-parity surface magnetism in a Kondo insulator
papers.abstract: We formulate a theory of spin-polarized tunneling between a nanowire tip of a topological Kondo insulator SmB$_6$ and the bi-collinear antiferromagnet Fe$_{1+x}$Te in which the tunneling conductance which measures magnetic contrast changes sign when the bias is reversed. First we show that no time reversal symmetric tip, however strong its spin-momentum locking is, can produce experimentally observed magnetic contrast, which implies that time reversal must be broken at the tip surface. Within a mean-field treatment of the surface theory of SmB$_6$ we find that the interaction between conduction d-and f-electrons drives a surface phase transition near T$_c$ ~10 K in which the time reversal odd component of the Kondo hybridization amplitude condenses in the same symmetry channel as an out-of-plane surface magnetization, gapping out the Dirac surface states. Below the transition the spin-resolved spectral function of each gapped surface Dirac cone is odd in energy about its node. For a charge-neutral apex the Fermi level lies between the surface $Γ$ and $X$ Dirac nodes, so the spin-polarized conductance, which is determined by this function at the bias energy, reverses its sign close to zero bias. This sign change is thus a spectroscopic signature of time reversal symmetry breaking on the surface of SmB6.

papers.title: Enhanced Coulomb pseudopotentials in high-pressure hydrides from first principles
papers.abstract: In the Eliashberg theory of superconductivity, Coulomb interactions oppose the phonon-mediated attraction and suppress the superconducting critical temperature $T_{\mathrm{c}}$. However, most first-principles predictions continue to treat this repulsion with an empirical Coulomb pseudopotential $μ^*_{\text{ME}}$ in the range 0.1-0.15. Here we present first-principles calculations of the Coulomb parameter $μ$ and pseudopotential $μ^*_{\text{ME}}$ in superconducting hydrides across a range of pressures. The screened Coulomb interaction is evaluated at the random phase approximation level with the Mantel code. We demonstrate that several hydride systems, including H$_3$S, YSbH$_6$ and Mg$_2$IrH$_6$, have strong Coulomb repulsions driven by a large density of states at the Fermi energy, $N_{\mathrm{F}}$. For Mg$_2$IrH$_6$ we obtain $μ=0.62$ and $μ^*_{\text{ME}}\approx0.39$, leading to a 40 K suppression in $T_{\mathrm{c}}$ relative to a standard $μ^*_{\text{ME}}=0.16$. Our obtained $μ^*_{\text{ME}}$ is far above the conventional range and, accounting for the energy dependence of the density of states, resolves the factor-of-two discrepancy between $T_{\mathrm{c}}$ estimates of previous studies. Across all systems and pressures studied, we find that $μ$ closely tracks $N_{\mathrm{F}}$, suggesting that commonly used $μ^*_{\text{ME}}$ values lead to overestimated $T_{\mathrm{c}}$ in materials where the density of states at the Fermi energy is large.

papers.title: Frustrated Topological Orbital Magnetism
papers.abstract: By studying the interplay of geometric frustration with Aharonov-Bohm fluxes in three dimensions, we unveil a rich playground exhibiting topological semimetallic ground states with orbital magnetic dipole, quadrupole and ferrotoroidic orders, akin to spin patterns in classical spin ices - a class of phenomena which we dub frustrated topological orbital magnetism. We demonstrate that the ground-state toroidizations underpinned by non-Abelian topological nodal lines induce measurable current-induced Hall phenomena. We further find that distinct 2-in-2-out and 3-in-1-out frustrated orbital current patterns can be associated with topological Weyl node charges, and corresponding anisotropic linear and nonlinear Hall effects. We propose signatures for experimental validation of distinct frustrated topological orbital magnetic orders in candidate materials.

papers.title: Flat-band quantum geometry from embedded quench dynamics
papers.abstract: Quantum geometry underlies a wide range of correlated phenomena in electronic systems, yet accessing the geometry of individual bands remains experimentally challenging. Advances in quantum simulators, such as ultracold atoms in optical lattices, have enabled local state preparation and site-resolved measurements, offering direct access to quantum dynamics beyond conventional transport probes. These developments naturally raise the question of whether band-resolved quantum geometry can be extracted from local occupation readouts. Here, we propose an on-site quench protocol to probe the flat-band quantum geometry via local occupation measurements in an atomic lattice. Our scheme dynamically isolates the flat-band sector by coupling a one-dimensional flat-band lattice to a two-dimensional flat-band bath. The bath selectively removes dispersive excitations, while compact localized states remain trapped due to their overlap with the flat-band modes of the bath. We show that the late-time occupation pattern directly encodes the integrated overlaps between flat-band states separated by the wavevector of the initial density pattern, thereby enabling access to integrated quantum distances between the states separated by the commensurate momenta $δk = 2 πs/r$, $s,r \in \mathbb Z$ and to the integrated flat-band quantum metric. Our results thereby establish a direct connection between quantum geometry and the long-time memory of an initial spatial pattern in flat-band systems.

papers.title: Spinodal-controlled freeze-out and nucleation at the first-order superfluid-supersolid transition of a dipolar gas
papers.abstract: Dipolar quantum gases in elongated traps become supersolid through a transition that is continuous at intermediate density but first order at low and high density; at the continuous point, ramps of the scattering length follow Kibble--Zurek scaling. We study ramps across the first-order superfluid--supersolid transition of $^{164}$Dy in an infinite tube using the three-dimensional extended Gross--Pitaevskii equation with truncated-Wigner noise. With quantum noise only, the uniform superfluid survives the metastable window and transforms after its spinodal, where the roton softens. For onsets occurring during the linear ramp, the delay measured from this spinodal has a fitted exponent $ζ= 0.36 \pm 0.02$, close to the continuous-transition result and the mean-field value $1/3$. The quoted uncertainty combines statistical and systematic sensitivities. Reverse ramps show a comparable delay beyond the fold of the crystal branch, producing dynamical hysteresis. Initial thermal noise with nominal temperatures of 2.5--10 nK produces crystalline regions inside the metastable window during holds, with faster nucleation closer to the spinodal and at higher initial temperature. Without a heat bath these effective rates depend on preparation: ramps crossing the window at the same rate nucleate early in 2 of 32 or 11 of 16 realizations depending on their starting point. A crossover time inferred from hold rates is therefore an estimate, not a measured boundary for the ramp protocol. At low density, slower ramps select larger spacings in a crystal of separated droplets, and droplets survive far above the transition on reverse ramps.

papers.title: Cooper Instability of a Magnetic Wigner Crystal
papers.abstract: Recent scanning tunneling microscopy has directly imaged electronic crystals in rhombohedral hexalayer graphene, and magnetotransport measurements suggest that superconductivity and charge-density-wave order emerge from a common spin-valley-polarized ferromagnetic metal at nearby carrier densities. Motivated by these observations, we ask whether collective modes in a magnetic Wigner crystal can mediate pairing in this setting. We address this question by studying the Cooper problem for two electrons in the first conduction band of the Wigner crystal. Unlike conventional phonon-mediated pairing, the collective mode (boson) energies and single-particle (fermion) dispersion are comparable scales controlled by the electron density, leaving no small parameter for an adiabatic expansion. Moreover, because the magnetic Wigner crystal is not time-reversal invariant, the usual Cooper logarithmic divergence in the pairing susceptibility is absent, so the attraction must exceed a finite threshold for pairing to occur. These unusual features motivate a numerical experiment to see whether the crystal's own vibrations can bind electrons. We obtain the crystalline ground state and its collective mode spectrum within Hartree--Fock and time-dependent Hartree--Fock approximation, and derive the electron--phonon Hamiltonian using the quasiboson approximation. Solving the resulting two-electron problem, we find that phonon-mediated attraction exceeds the pairing threshold, with chiral $p$-wave pairing as the leading instability. Within these approximations, we show that collective modes of a Wigner crystal can indeed favor chiral pairing despite broken time-reversal symmetry. Our results provide an encouraging starting point for developing a full many-body theory to study electronic crystallization and superconductivity.

papers.title: Surface scalar plasmons on curved interfaces: a venue for analogue gravity
papers.abstract: We investigate whether the geometry of a curved conductor--dielectric interface can modify the effective mass and propagation of scalar surface plasmons (SSPs). In the hydrodynamic limit, we describe SSPs as density perturbations in a semiclassical jellium electron gas. Using a thin--layer dimensional reduction procedure, we derive a massive Klein--Gordon equation for SSPs on the curved interface with a geometric potential. We find that under specific conditions, the geometric potential allows SSP propagation with a vanishing effective mass. We then apply the formalism to a well known analogue black hole configuration, determining the corresponding quasinormal mode frequencies. Our results show that interface curvature provides a geometric handle on plasmon propagation and localization, suggesting new possibilities for plasmon transport and analogue gravity experiments with surface plasmons.

papers.title: An entangling Hubbard quasiparticle collider on a digital quantum processor
papers.abstract: Scattering of quasiparticles provides direct access to the interactions that govern strongly correlated systems. In this work, we realize the quasiparticle scattering experiment of the Fermi-Hubbard model on a digital quantum processor by colliding a doublon and a holon in the half-filled chain of 21 sites encoded on 42 qubits of the ibm_boston processor. For the first time, we measure the transmission probability of quasiparticles of the Hubbard model on quantum hardware, which agrees with the Bethe-ansatz scattering matrix without free parameters. Beyond the scattering probabilities, the collision generates entanglement by superposing the transmitted and reflected components, which we infer from the particle-number fluctuation. In sharp contrast, a control collision between two doublons shows neither the interaction dependence nor the number fluctuation, as expected for indistinguishable particles. Our work demonstrates that the ability to create quasiparticles of a chosen flavor on demand and program their motion and interactions makes a digital quantum processor a new experimental toolset for probing the entanglement structure generated by quasiparticle scattering.

papers.title: A Warped Born Rule Turns an Observer into a Maxwell's Demon
papers.abstract: Quantum mechanics seems to be an incredibly delicate theory. Slight alterations to nearly any part of its structure can lead to huge qualitative differences and wildly unphysical predictions. Here, we explore the many-body consequences of replacing the Born rule $p(m)\propto\|P_m|ψ\rangle|^2$ by a warped rule $p_b(m)\propto\|P_m|ψ\rangle\|^{2b}$. Specifically, in systems with conserved particle number, evolution punctuated by repeated local particle observations acquires a probabilistic bias over measurement histories with an effect controlled by the sign of $b-1$. For $b>1$, this bias generically drives the gas to collect into nearly frozen configurations. Similar to the action of Maxwell's demon, the simple act of observation seems to extract entropy from a closed system. For $b<1$, the bias is reversed, generically scouring out long-wavelength fluctuations to produce a hyperuniform gas. We study this effect in a one-dimensional quantum gas, where these two phases are derived analytically for a particular measurement scheme and corroborated numerically for more general procedures with discrete-time projective-measurement circuit models using matrix product state simulations. We additionally discuss how this bias manifests in a common technique that often employs this warped rule, the ``replica trick,'' implying qualitative differences between finite-replica and replica-limit calculations.

papers.title: $q$-deformed Weil-Petersson Volumes from the Spectral Edge of DSSYK and Supersymmetric Extensions
papers.abstract: The $q$-deformed Weil-Petersson volumes of Do and Norbury are the top-degree parts of Okuyama's discrete volumes, which are defined by topological recursion on the spectral curve of the double-scaled SYK (DSSYK) model. We show that the same q-deformed volumes can be obtained from a double-scaled matrix model whose disk density is found by zooming in on the soft edges of the DSSYK density. Applying the same procedure to the hard edge of $\mathcal{N}=1$ DSSYK, we obtain candidate $q$-deformed $\mathcal{N}=1$ super Weil-Petersson volumes. They are polynomials of fixed degree, and they reduce to the $\mathcal{N}=1$ super Weil-Petersson volumes in a scaled $q\to1$ limit. These candidate volumes differ from the $\mathcal{N}=1$ volumes of Do and Norbury in (arXiv:2510.12431) up to what we call "irrelevant" contributions which exactly vanish in the scaled $q\to 1$ limit. Together, these results demonstrate how q-deformed volumes can be naturally associated to the spectral edges of various DSSYK models and provides an intuitive way to construct them in supersymmetric contexts.

papers.title: Modular Properties of Generalised Gibbs Ensembles: The Deformed KdV Hierarchy
papers.abstract: We construct a set of conserved charges which are deformations of quantum KdV charges. They are associated with the modular transformation of a GGE with the spin-$σ$ KdV charge inserted with chemical potential $α_σ$. The charges are formal power series in the chemical potential, with coefficients given by local integrals of motion. We define local recursion relations and equivalent flow equations, prove commutativity to all orders, and establish uniqueness of the currents modulo total derivatives for a fixed generating series. We show that the eigenvalues of these deformed charges can be obtained from the thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz in two models. In the $c=1/2$ free fermion theory, the deformed charges reduce to explicit linear combinations of undeformed KdV charges, and their ground-state eigenvalues agree with the TBA expansion to all orders. In the Lee-Yang model, we find numerical agreement through cubic order in the spin-$5$ deformation for the first few charges evaluated on low-lying states.

papers.title: Locality-Preparation Time Tradeoffs in Dissipative Quantum Systems
papers.abstract: Dissipative state preparation engineers quantum many-body states as steady states of an open-system dynamics. The spatial range of the required dissipation sets both the feasibility of analog implementations and the connectivity and control complexity of digital ones. Yet how this locality quantitatively constrains preparation times remains largely unknown. Here, we establish an exact locality-preparation time relation for quadratic fermionic systems and develop a construction that optimizes the locality of the dissipative dynamics while preserving the target state. Applied to the Kitaev chain, our framework reveals sharply different locality-preparation time tradeoffs in critical and gapped regimes. At criticality, suppressing the algebraic tails of the jump operators necessarily forces the preparation time to grow algebraically with system size. By contrast, both trivial and topological gapped phases admit exponentially localized dissipation with a finite preparation time in the thermodynamic limit. Our results identify when fast dissipative preparation is compatible with local control and when criticality imposes an unavoidable dynamical cost.

papers.title: Utilizing Neural Networks for Solving Functional Renormalization Group Flow Equations
papers.abstract: A novel physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) based approach for solving functional renormalization group flow equations is presented. We investigate the finite temperature phase transition in $O(N)$ models without relying on the large-$N$ approximation, which was used in earlier attempts with similar methods. We argue that these previous solutions cannot easily be generalized for more complex symmetries, and hence our approach can provide new insight. Our technique relies on a series of ansätze that combines the small- and large-field approximation schemes with a neural network, leading to a highly accurate approximation over the entire field range. We compare the PINNs approach with traditional grid-based Runge-Kutta results and show that the network can successfully learn the temperature, field, and scale dependencies of the effective potential in the local potential approximation.

papers.title: Anomaly induced transport in holographic superconductors
papers.abstract: We investigate the anomaly-induced transport properties of a holographic superconductor exhibiting spontaneous symmetry breaking. The holographic model incorporates vector and axial gauge fields, an additional non-anomalous $U(1)$ symmetry, and a charged scalar field that drives the phase transition. Working in the probe limit, we numerically construct the superconducting background under two alternative scalar field quantizations, corresponding to operators with scaling dimensions $Δ=1$ and $Δ=3$ (denoted as the $O_1$ and $O_2$ theories, respectively). Using Kubo formulae, we compute the chiral magnetic conductivities and examine their response to the scalar condensate. Our findings demonstrate that spontaneous symmetry breaking allows anomaly-induced transport to extend beyond anomalous currents, significantly impacting the non-anomalous sector as well. Remarkably, this effect appears in both theories, indicating that the influence on the non-anomalous sector is independent of the chosen quantization. The comparison of our numerical results with the analytical limits for $O_i \to 0$ and $O_i \to \infty$ $(i=1,2)$ reveals consistent behavior across both theories.

papers.title: Encoding Matters: A Qubit-Efficient Reformulation for Quantum Resilient Routing
papers.abstract: Qubits are powerful computational resources because each additional qubit doubles the size of the accessible state space. This expressive power comes at a cost: adding qubits also increases circuit size, constraint overhead, and exposure to hardware noise. These limitations are especially critical for near-term quantum computers, making the number of qubits required to formulate a problem a central practical concern. In this work, we present a method for efficiently mapping logistics and routing problems onto qubits through structure-aware encoding reduction. We demonstrate the method on a benchmark problem of latency-resilient routing under dual-link failures. For this benchmark, the reduced formulation substantially lowers both the qubit count and the compiled circuit complexity while preserving the original optimization task. By running the reduced model on the same trapped-ion quantum computer as the benchmark, we obtain a 100X improvement in the success probability. This finding shows how careful problem formulation can make current quantum hardware substantially more effective for practical optimization.

papers.title: Predicting the Final Stationary State of Sheared 2D Euler Fluids
papers.abstract: The Kelvin-Helmholtz (KH) instability is a fundamental signature of the natural world, manifesting in phenomena ranging from atmospheric clouds to the iconic turbulence of Jupiter's Great Red Spot. While the linear dynamics of this instability is well-understood, the ultimate fate of the fluid --- the final stationary state to which it relaxes --- remains a formidable challenge. In this paper, we present a general non-equilibrium statistical mechanics framework that allows us to predict the asymptotic vorticity distribution of a sheared 2D Euler fluid. By constructing a self-consistent ansatz for the solution of the Vlasov equation, we determine the stationary stream function without explicitly solving the time-dependent Euler equations. We demonstrate that the relaxation leads to a population-inverted core, where high-energy states are fully occupied, surrounded by a tenuous halo of vortices in the lower-energy regions of configuration space. This result establishes the core-halo structure as a robust statistical consequence of the system's evolution, offering a universal framework for understanding the saturation of shear-induced turbulence in inviscid 2D fluids.

papers.title: Some remarks on the connection between generative diffusion and optimal transport
papers.abstract: We discuss three simple connections between generative diffusion and optimal transport. First, the joint law of the data and of their Ornstein-Uhlenbeck noising is, at every time, the solution of an entropic optimal-transport problem, at a temperature set by the noise level. Backward diffusion can consequently be read as an annealing which gradually decreases the entropic regularization. Second, we study the speciation transition--how the modes of the data distribution emerge during generation--and compare how it happens in diffusion and flow matching with respect to optimal transport. Using Gaussian mixtures as high-dimensional example, we show that the dynamical instability through which diffusion and flow matching separate the modes becomes, for optimal transport, an exponentially thin boundary layer at the beginning of generation, which is rounded by entropic regularization. Third, considering a generic forward dynamics with a general confining potential, we show that the backward process driven by the score also satisfies a drift-based variational principle whose minimal cost is the entropy difference between initial and final distributions.

papers.title: Efficient Transport Networks through Edge Pruning by Relative Resistance
papers.abstract: Transport networks are key to living and engineered systems. How can transport networks adapt efficiently using only local rules, without a global objective or specific boundary conditions? Inspired by observations in biological transport networks, we adapt networks by subsequently pruning edges by relative resistance, thus removing edges whose resistance is higher than the resistance for routing flow through the rest of the network. We find that adaptation by such a local, boundary-condition-free measure of redundancy, set by topology alone, yields sparse, loop-rich, low-dissipation networks.

papers.title: Aubry-André transition in photonic time quasicrystals
papers.abstract: In one dimension, Anderson localization by a disordered potential sets in at any strength, whereas localization by a quasiperiodic potential in the Aubry-André model occurs through a transition at a critical strength. Disordered photonic time crystals exhibit a temporal counterpart of this Anderson localization, in which light, instead of decaying in space, stops propagating and grows in time. Whether a counterpart of the Aubry-André transition exists in photonic time quasicrystals remains an open question. Here we show that it does, and that the transition occurs at mobility edges in momentum rather than in energy. These edges arise even under impulsive modulation, where the field obeys the self-dual almost-Mathieu equation exactly, and for general analytic modulations Avila's global theory reveals the condition under which they form. The Aubry-André transition thus extends from spatial lattices to the time domain, where it sorts light by wave number into components that propagate and components that stop and grow.

papers.title: Modelling Josephson Junctions with Boundary Conditions: Towards High-Fidelity Models for Superconducting Qubits
papers.abstract: Josephson junctions are the central nonlinear element of superconducting qubits, yet their standard description is reached through a chain of approximations. We propose a purely quantum-mechanical model of the junction, formulated directly in Hilbert space: a charged particle moves on a one-dimensional loop, and the junction is a point at which the wave function obeys self-adjoint boundary conditions, labelled by a coupling strength $λ$, which controls the transparency of the junction, and a phase jump $δ$, which plays the role of the superconducting phase difference. For a loop with a single junction we solve the spectral problem and show that the ground-state momentum expectation, identified with the supercurrent, factorises exactly as $\langle\hat{p}_0\rangle = I_c(δ,λ)\sinδ$. For opaque junctions $I_c$ becomes independent of $δ$ and the first Josephson relation $I=I_c\sinδ$ is recovered; for strongly attractive coupling, where the ground state is bound to the junction, the $\sinδ$ law is also recovered, but with an exponentially suppressed amplitude. For more transparent junctions, however, the model \emph{predicts} deviations from the pure $\sinδ$ law: $I_c$ acquires a dependence on $δ$ already at order $λ^{-2}$, compatible with the higher Josephson harmonics recently found necessary to describe superconducting qubit spectra, and a fully transparent contact yields a current linear in $δ$. When the phase varies in time, a gauge transformation shows that the voltage drop across the junction is proportional to $\dotδ$, so that the second Josephson relation emerges without being imposed. The boundary-condition approach thus reproduces both Josephson relations from first principles and predicts corrections to them, offering a route towards higher-fidelity models of superconducting qubits.

papers.title: Zak Phase Quantization without Global Symmetry through Destructive Interference
papers.abstract: The Zak phase provides a fundamental geometric characterization of one-dimensional band structures and, when quantized by symmetry, serves as a bulk indicator of polarization and boundary phenomena. Conventionally, its exact quantization is tied to a global symmetry of the Bloch Hamiltonian, such as inversion or reflection symmetry. Here, we demonstrate a distinct mechanism by which the Zak phase remains exactly quantized even when the corresponding protecting symmetry is explicitly broken at the level of the full Hamiltonian. The mechanism is based on local support symmetry and destructive interference: symmetry-breaking degrees of freedom are coupled to a topological parent system in such a way that the relevant Bloch states cannot leak into them. The preserved states therefore retain their parent wave functions and inherit their quantized Zak phase exactly, despite the absence of the protecting global symmetry. We establish this mechanism for general one-dimensional insulators and demonstrate it in an inversion-broken minimal model and a reflection-broken armchair nanoribbon, where a quantized $π$ Zak phase and associated boundary-localized states persist. We further show that perturbations violating the exact destructive-interference condition continuously dequantize the Zak phase, while a finite regime with a near-$π$ Zak phase and boundary response can survive. Our results establish wave-function support, rather than global symmetry alone, as a mechanism for protecting quantized quantum geometry in one-dimensional systems.

papers.title: Percolation of Data Constraints and Reorganization of Boolean Function States in Parity Learning
papers.abstract: We study how a neural network reorganizes its learned function as training proceeds and as previously unseen parity data accumulate. The trained model is itself a Boolean function on binary strings of finite length. We then evaluate it on all data, inside and outside the training set, and read off its complete sign table. Its $\pm1$ entries are the amplitudes of a normalized state, dubbed the function-state, whose inverse subsystem purity $K_f=1/\textrm{Tr}(ρ_A^2)$ is an effective Schmidt rank. We find that small data additions broaden the Schmidt spectrum, whereas larger additions reconcentrate it in the target mode. The former is called differentiation because the model distinguishes inputs more sharply. The latter is called target-selective recoherence, where the model settles on the single rule shared by the added data. As the dataset grows, the connectivity of the constraint graph defined by the training set increases monotonically, whereas the learned inverse purity changes nonmonotonically. On a fixed connected dataset, as learning proceeds, the Schmidt spectrum begins to reorganize, followed by gains in target alignment and later by improvement in predictive accuracy. This ordering distinguishes three aspects of learning: constraint identifiability, function-state organization, and predictive accuracy. At fixed data size, a function that has already been learned can re-differentiate, an event we call retreat, without changing graph connectivity. Recovery reconcentrates the Schmidt spectrum in a similar target-selective pattern, without exact recurrence of the Boolean state. Thus the percolation of data constraints fixes the identifiable support, while the reduced state produced by training continues to reorganize even after that support stops changing.

papers.title: When irrelevance governs: dissipation-regression scaling in open quantum criticality
papers.abstract: The real-time dynamics of quantum phase transitions in open systems coupled to finite-temperature environments sits at the heart of contemporary condensed-matter and quantum-information science. Here, invoking a Schwinger-Keldysh formalism, we uncover that, within the coherence-dominated regime of critical real-time evolution, a dissipative coupling deemed naively irrelevant determines, counterintuitively, the longest timescale that holds sway. Possessing a well-defined temporal scaling dimension, it engenders a novel dissipation-regression scaling that systematically reproduces the unusual Kibble-Zurek scaling and relaxation observed in recent numerical studies. By contrast, dissipation-dominated dynamics behaves qualitatively differently. There, furthermore, we show that the discretized and diagonalized formulations of the same open quantum Ising chain realize distinct universality classes.

papers.title: An Instability of the Quantum Markov Length
papers.abstract: The Markov length, the length scale governing the exponential decay of conditional mutual information (CMI) in a quantum many-body state, has proven useful for characterizing mixed-state phases of matter. Nevertheless, we show that a state's Markov length is not generally stable under weak local channels. The failure of stability occurs already at a pure product state. We demonstrate this explicitly in a one-dimensional fermionic chain, where a fine-tuned depth-two circuit of nearest-neighbor Gaussian channels maps the vacuum to a state whose CMI decays \emph{algebraically} and whose Markov length is therefore infinite, even when the channels are taken arbitrarily close to the identity. The algebraic decay is rooted in the nonanalyticity of the von Neumann entropy at rank-deficient density operators. We exhibit an analogous instability on an ordinary qubit chain. More generally, we show that the Markov length is unstable in any translation-invariant state with even a single rank-deficient reduced density operator. These results pose a challenge to recent definitions of mixed-state phase equivalence based on the Markov length.

papers.title: Alter-excitons in Altermagnets: Symmetry, Splitting and Dispersion
papers.abstract: Magnetism provides a fertile platform for discovering emergent quantum phenomena governed by symmetry. Recent developments of spin-space-group (SSG) theory have revealed altermagnets as a distinct class of nonrelativistic collinear magnets with unconventional spin-dependent electronic structures. Here, we demonstrate that altermagnetic symmetry imposes fundamentally different constraints on electronic and excitonic excitations. Although the quasiparticle and two-body Hamiltonians possess identical SSG symmetries, we find that symmetry-protected degeneracies present in the electronic band structure can be intrinsically lifted in the exciton spectrum at specific momenta. This splitting arises solely from the many-body nature of excitons and does not require spin-orbit coupling or noncollinear magnetic order. Combining symmetry analysis with many-body perturbation theory, we predict a novel class of spin-split excitonic quasiparticles, termed alter-excitons, and reveal their characteristic dispersions in altermagnetic systems. Our results establish excitons as a sensitive probe of hidden spin-space symmetries and uncover a new route toward symmetry-engineered many-body phenomena in collinear magnets.

papers.title: Analog quantum simulation of Shastry-Sutherland Ising materials
papers.abstract: Frustrated magnets host rich emergent behavior because competing interactions generate dense manifolds of low-energy states. The Ising Shastry-Sutherland model is a paradigmatic setting, motivated experimentally by Ising-like rare-earth tetraborides such as TmB$_4$ and ErB$_4$, whose field-induced magnetization plateaus have motivated extensive microscopic modeling. Yet how tunable quantum fluctuations reorganize this material-motivated phase diagram remains largely unexplored. Here, we realize a transverse- and longitudinal-field Ising model on the Shastry-Sutherland lattice using a programmable Rydberg-atom array. We map its quantum phase diagram using density matrix renormalization group calculations and probe corresponding signatures experimentally in arrays containing more than 110 atoms. Beyond the established classical phases, the calculations identify two regimes absent in the classical limit and stabilized at finite transverse field: a $2/5$ filling plateau whose finite stability region emerges from a classically degenerate phase boundary and a symmetry-preserving quantum-dimer regime replacing classically selected collinear order. Experiments on finite open arrays reveal signatures consistent with these regimes across three boundary-pinning conditions, with the resulting response maps agreeing qualitatively with the calculated phase diagram. Our results establish programmable Rydberg-atom arrays as tools for exploring frustrated, material-motivated Hamiltonians and motivate searches for new, quantum-driven magnetization plateaus and quantum-dimer behavior in ErB$_4$ under a transverse field or in strain-tuned TmB$_4$.

papers.title: Predictive Synthesis of MOFs and COFs
papers.abstract: Predictive synthesis concerns the prospective modeling of how a targeted structure can be realized. The synthesis of metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) and covalent organic frameworks (COFs) intrinsically involves a multidimensional space of interdependent variables, posing a challenge for bench chemists to parameterize and predict. In this Perspective, we discuss the evolution from chemical-intuition-driven experimentation toward the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) in the laboratory. By virtue of prior knowledge, uncertainty, and experimental failure in determining what should be attempted next, we envision predictive synthesis progressing from static recipe recommendation toward real-time control and transferable principles of framework formation. In this context, the significance lies in transforming trial-and-error practice into a means of measurable chemical reasoning, thereby accelerating crystalline materials discovery and advancing synthetic chemistry.

papers.title: Tropical QFT and the sine-Gordon model
papers.abstract: A tropical quantum field theory is an exactly solvable deformation limit of an ordinary QFT, governed by a non-linear partial differential equation. We use the integrable two-dimensional sine-Gordon theory as a testbench to compare the exact features of an undeformed model with its tropical counterpart. We classify scale-invariant tropical QFTs in $D=2$ and leverage functional renormalization group methods to demonstrate that all scale-invariant theories with periodic effective actions are infrared fixed points of flows originating from sine-Gordon Lagrangians. For the tropical sine-Gordon model, we compute the $β$-functions exactly, solve the renormalized theory both via a convergent expansion and numerically for all admissible couplings, and illustrate the complete renormalization group flow from the Gaussian to the IR fixed point. Finally, we study the large-order behaviour of the loop expansion and relate it to the Hamilton-Jacobi equation, whose solutions we interpret as tropical instantons.

papers.title: Dissipative Majorana Chain---Anomalies and Non-Invertible Symmetries
papers.abstract: We study symmetries and anomalies of dissipative Majorana chains described by Lindblad dynamics. Using the operator-state mapping, we represent the Lindbladian as a non-Hermitian operator on a doubled Hilbert space. In this formulation, the ket and bra contours admit strong fermion parities and strong translations, while their diagonal combinations define weak symmetries. For even and odd chain lengths, we diagnose anomalies by comparing symmetry algebras with and without weak fermion-parity defects. These algebras retain the lattice precursor of the modulo-$8$ anomaly of the closed Majorana chain and exhibit projective relations between strong fermion parity and weak translation, as well as between weak fermion parity and strong translation, which are intrinsic to open quantum systems. We establish the IR correspondence between the lattice symmetry algebras and those of the doubled Majorana CFT in four spin sectors, identifying chiral fermion parities emanated from the lattice translations. Finally, we develop the lattice bosonization of the dissipative chain. For even length with collective energy dephasing, combining the defect and no-defect sectors and imposing GSO projections gives rise to an Ising Lindbladian with non-invertible Kramers--Wannier symmetries descending from the anomalous strong translation and fermion parity of the Majorana chain. For odd length, constructing mutually commuting ket- and bra-sector spin operators instead yields an Ising Lindbladian with a Kramers--Wannier duality defect. Our results provide a controlled framework for extending lattice anomalies and non-invertible symmetries to open quantum systems.

papers.title: Error correction and quantum information spreading on sparse random graphs
papers.abstract: Quantum error-correcting codes on graph geometries beyond regular euclidean lattices have emerged as a promising route toward robust quantum information processing. A major challenge in quantum error correction is the trade-off between favorable properties of codes constructed in high dimensionality and the need for locality in practical implementations on near-term hardware. Sparse intermediate geometries may combine the advantages of both, but how their structure governs quantum information dynamics and code performance remains unclear. Here we show that the spectral dimension $d_s$, defined from the low-energy spectrum of the graph Laplacian, is the universal parameter connecting these properties. Using Floquet random Clifford circuits on two distinct sparse graph architectures with tunable spectral dimension, we find that $d_s$ governs both quantum information spreading and the scaling of the resulting quantum error-correcting code distance. We identify a geometry-induced entanglement phase transition from localized area-law to ergodic volume-law, whose universality is determined by $d_s$ and exhibits long-range percolation criticality. In the ergodic phase, the circuit acts as a CSS code encoder whose code distance is set by the competition between two logical sectors --- the cost of severing the graph and the length of its shortest winding cycle --- which connectivity pushes in opposite directions. The spectral dimension organizes this trade-off, highlighting a maximum at intermediate $d_s$ retaining sparse connectivity and physical realizability.

papers.title: Correlated Pair Creation with Positive- and Negative-Frequency Oscillators in a Trapped-Ion Quantum Simulator
papers.abstract: Spin-dependent forces enable independent control over the effective frequencies of bosonic motional modes and their coupling strengths to spins in trapped-ion spin-boson quantum simulators. We show that the relative signs of these effective frequencies provide an important programmable resource for engineering distinct multimode dynamics. Focusing on a two-mode quantum Rabi model, changing the frequencies of the two modes from the same sign to opposite signs reorganizes the resonance structure of the spin-mediated bosonic interaction, converting the dominant resonant process from excitation exchange to correlated pair creation. In the dispersive regime, the resulting effective interaction realizes a two-mode parametric amplifier with stable oscillatory, critical, and exponentially amplifying regimes separated by a spin-dependent instability threshold. Across these regimes, the dynamics generate collective-quadrature squeezing and bipartite motional entanglement. Preparing the spin in a coherent superposition further allows different spin components to experience distinct stability regimes, generating tripartite spin-boson entanglement, while spin postselection can coherently combine the conditional bosonic branches to generate non-Gaussian entangled bosonic states. Finally, we outline an implementation using parameters within reach of current trapped-ion platforms.

papers.title: Separating Field--Camp Alignment from Structural Balance in a Frustrated Random-Field Ising Model of Social Networks
papers.abstract: Frustrated Ising models of social networks mix ferromagnetic (agreement-seeking) and antiferromagnetic (antagonistic) couplings, and the antagonistic bonds are almost always placed independently at a fixed rate, yielding a +/-J spin glass. Real signed networks (Epinions, Slashdot, Wikipedia) instead show an excess of balanced triads, and perfectly balanced placement is gauge-equivalent to an unfrustrated ferromagnet. We compare three sign-placement conditions on a frustrated random-field Ising model of a polarised population, sharing an identical graph, field assignment, and edge-weight magnitudes: an independent baseline; a balance-structured condition whose camp membership coincides with each voter's field sign; and the same condition with camp labels randomly permuted, so triadic balance is identical by construction while the camp-field correlation is removed. On a confound-controlled Kolmogorov-Smirnov test of the sampled energy-gap distribution (simulated annealing), the aligned condition differs from the baseline at every density tested (p = 7.3e-8), while the permuted condition shows no significant difference (paired mean difference 0.003, 95% CI [-0.041, 0.046]). Field-camp alignment, not triadic balance alone, drives the effect. The qualitative direction follows from a known mapping; the contribution is a quantitative, confound-controlled measurement of the effect's size away from that limit, robust to parallel-tempering sampling, system sizes up to N = 300, and structural noise calibrated to real networks, while triadic balance alone produces no detectable effect at N = 90 and at most a small one at N = 180-300 (paired change in KS distance about 0.04, 95% CI upper bound below 0.09).

papers.title: An all-transistor physical-learning transformer can be trained to perform in-context learning
papers.abstract: Most systems trained by equilibrium propagation or coupled learning are in the same class as multi-layer perceptrons: while they may be universal function approximators, they struggle to learn associative tasks which are easy for transformers. Equilibrium propagation relies on a bidirectional flow of information through the physical system between input and output. The reverse flow is broken by more complex nonlinear systems, such as those performing multiplication which is needed to express dot-product attention. Here we explicitly restore this bidirectional flow by introducing extra circuit elements for this purpose into a double or dyadic circuit. We then use these ideas to construct an attention mechanism exploiting the exponential current law of sub-threshold MOSFET devices. We show that in simulations this circuit can be trained to perform a simple in-context learning task, despite using realistic reverse components which transmit only an approximate gradient. For this training to succeed we need cross-entropy loss (not mean squared error). We generate nudges appropriate for this loss using a novel floating circuit element, based on the same MOSFET sub-circuit used for softmax. We train the resistors in this circuit using the Lion optimiser, which can be implemented using one capacitor per parameter to store local memory of past gradient estimates.

papers.title: Quantum limit to transparency
papers.abstract: We argue that no material can be made completely transparent to light as long as it has a nontrivial index of refraction. The quantum decay of photons into phonons is an ineliminable source of attenuation. This survives even once all other excitations have been gapped away, impurities have been removed, and the temperature has been set to zero. Restricting for simplicity to the case of a superfluid, we determine via effective field theory methods the corresponding low-frequency contribution to the imaginary part of the index of refraction. This scales as $ω^4$ and induces a nonanalyticity of the real part for $ω\rightarrow 0$. We also extend our result to large coherent electromagnetic fields, such as those of a laser, showing that the effect can receive strong nonlinear enhancements. Our result is a genuine quantum lower bound to the transparency of a medium.

papers.title: Exact solutions of non-Markovian dissipative Ising models
papers.abstract: Applications of quantum devices and simulators require an accurate understanding of their dynamics as well as the effects of environmental noise. While some sources of noise can be modeled as Markovian dissipation, coupling to resonators or vibrational modes often produces non-Markovian dynamics as well, making it difficult to characterize the system, particularly for interacting many-body systems. Here, we identify a broad class of exactly solvable many-body quantum systems with both non-Markovian dynamics and Markovian dissipation. We consider a prototypical model of spins coupled to lossy bosonic modes that mediate Ising-type interactions. We exclude a transverse field but allow local spin dissipation that need not commute with the interactions, including dephasing, relaxation, pumping, and even processes that generate coherences. Using an exact stochastic representation, we decouple the many-body dynamics into the evolution of individual spins, yielding exact spin observables and correlations without adiabatically eliminating the bosons. In the Markovian limit, our solutions describe Ising models with correlated dephasing and nonreciprocal interactions. An example of spin squeezing shows that both the achievable squeezing and its optimal preparation time depend strongly on the interplay between non-Markovian dynamics and Markovian dissipation.

papers.title: Why has PET glycolysis remained difficult to industrialize despite decades of optimization?
papers.abstract: Classical PET glycolysis struggles with industrial scale-up due to a research paradigm defect: uncoupled reaction optimization that ignores system-level engineering entropy. By establishing a governing reference frame, Scientific Reasoning Units (SRUs) and human-AI collaborative discovery in this article, we present a Three-Step Synergistic Reinforcement Paradigm addressing the triple failure modes of traditional systems-mass-transfer collapse, viscosity deadlock, and side-reaction accumulation. By integrating twin-screw controlled shearing, solid-state micro-homogenization, and deep depolymerization (2:1 EG/Oligomer ratio), we achieve an ultrafast kinetic regime. BHET yields surge to 80% to 95% within 10 minutes, eliminating multi-hour thermal bottlenecks and delivering an economically viable framework for closed-loop polyester recycling.

papers.title: Short-Range Vector Spin Glasses: Parisi Hierarchies and Real-Space Ultrametricity
papers.abstract: Replica symmetry breaking (RSB) is the organizing principle of mean-field spin-glass theory, yet whether a continuous Parisi hierarchy can arise in a genuinely short-range system in finite spatial dimension remains unresolved. Here we introduce a disordered model of $N$-component vector spins on a $D$-dimensional hypercubic lattice, with random matrix couplings on nearest-neighbor links and random tensor couplings on elementary plaquettes. In the large-$N$ limit, the model supports thermodynamically stable one-step, full, and one-full RSB phases, alongside replica-symmetric paramagnetic and ferromagnetic phases. We find that spatial locality constrains these ordered phases through two distinct infrared mechanisms. ($i$) Quenched random anisotropy destroys uniform ferromagnetism for $D\leq4$ through an Imry-Ma mechanism. ($ii$) A continuous Parisi hierarchy gives rise to replica Goldstone modes whose gaplessness is protected by a Ward identity. At leading order in $1/N$, these modes behave as a band of free spin waves, producing infrared-divergent fluctuations in $D\leq2$ and a Mermin-Wagner instability of the continuously broken phase. Remarkably, the Parisi hierarchy also acquires a direct real-space interpretation. For two pure states with mutual overlap $q$, a characteristic length $ξ(q)$ describes how far the differences between their frozen magnetization patterns remain correlated. Throughout a continuous sector of the Parisi hierarchy, $ξ(q)$ is independent of temperature and decreases monotonically with $q$. The ultrametric organization of pure states is therefore accompanied by an ultrametric hierarchy of real-space correlation lengths: states that separate near the root of the Parisi tree differ through long-wavelength frozen patterns, whereas states that separate farther from the root differ only on progressively shorter scales.

papers.title: Lyapunov spectrum of random neural networks
papers.abstract: The Lyapunov spectrum of a nonlinear recurrent neural network with random asymmetric couplings is calculated in the limit $N\to\infty$. The calculation is based on a finite-$N$ identity that expresses the cumulative distribution of Lyapunov exponents as a response function of the tangent-space dynamics, with the tangent trajectory selected by a minimum-norm condition rather than by an initial condition. A cavity method then determines this response function at large $N$ through a self-consistent single-site problem. This result establishes that the chaos in this network is extensive and gives access to diffeomorphism-invariant properties of the dynamics. This work was done in collaboration with the AI models GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5.

papers.title: Constructing Large and Structured Decoherence-Free Subspaces in Hybrid Quantum Systems
papers.abstract: We develop a framework to construct large decoherence-free subspaces with a non-trivial structure. The construction is based on hybrid quantum systems in which quantum matter is coupled to a dissipative bosonic mode. Dissipation imposes a global constraint on the matter by selecting the matter null states in the long-time limit. The decoherence-free subspaces spanned by matter null states can exhibit exotic quantum properties and emergent symmetries that do not characterize the full Liouvillian dynamics. We show how to construct many-body operators with physically interesting null states by employing representation theory of Lie algebras. This approach allows us to choose models based on their underlying algebraic structure. We consider explicitly the example of coupling a lossy optical cavity to the directed tunneling operator of quantum particles in one-dimension. In this case, the symmetries of the decoherence-free subspace originate in an $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb{C})$ algebra, leading to an exponentially large number of steady states. We characterize the null states for both fermionic and bosonic particles, employing analytical and numerical methods. The states exhibit several properties that underline their complex quantum nature: long-range kinetic correlations and volume-law entanglement. The nonreciprocal nature of the directed tunneling dynamics leads to the emergence in the many-body regime of a symmetry-constrained Liouvillian skin effect. The open light-matter system exhibits a strong symmetry stemming from spinless $η$-pairing algebras. We show how the non-trivial properties of the long-times states emerge in the dissipative dynamics from generic initial states, by performing time-dependent matrix product state simulations. Our framework opens avenues for dissipatively engineering complex quantum correlations and harnessing nonreciprocity in a controlled manner.

papers.title: True vs false Fermi surfaces in the Pseudogap regime and their transformation with doping and temperature in the Hubbard Model
papers.abstract: Exact diagrammatic quantum Monte Carlo (DiagMC) results for the nearest-neighbor Hubbard model motivate a closer study of the pseudogap. Using the improved two-particle self-consistent approach (TPSC+), we analyze Energy (EDC) and Momentum Distribution Curves (MDC) simultaneously. We show that Fermi-liquid terminology breaks down in the pseudogap regime, requiring a distinction between true and false Fermi surfaces and zero-energy quasiparticle (ZEQ) lines. A false Fermi surface has a momentum-space spectral maximum but a frequency-space depression at zero energy, while a false ZEQ line violates the standard quasiparticle condition $\partial Σ'(\mathbf{k},ω)/\partial ω|_{ω=0}<0$.The pseudogap is driven by critical thermal spin fluctuations, which occur in two dimensions because of the Mermin-Wagner theorem. Commensurate fluctuations first open an antinodal pseudogap, leaving true Fermi arcs. With decreasing temperature, the Fermi surface evolves into hole- and electron-like false Fermi surfaces. Incommensurate fluctuations generate hot spots near the diagonal, where the pseudogap persists to the quantum critical point (QCP), whereas at $\mathbf{k}_{AN}$ it disappears before the QCP doping. There, the spectrum has two precursor antiferromagnetic (AFM) bands, both in the unoccupied ($ω>0$) region. We benchmark TPSC+ against DiagMC results for the Matsubara spectral proxy $-\mathrm{Im}[\mathcal{G}(\mathbf{k},iπT)]/π$. TPSC+ underestimates pseudogap suppression in the strong-interaction regime, reproducing DiagMC behavior at lower temperatures or doping. This proxy is equivalent to the spectral function with thermal broadening $η=πT$, which obscures features when $πT$ is not the smallest energy scale. Using $A(\mathbf{k},0)$, we find that hole-like Fermi surfaces emerge at any interaction strength at low temperature, even at weak coupling.

papers.title: The Stability of Rutile Oxides for Oxygen Evolution Catalysis: From Mechanistic Understanding to New Descriptors
papers.abstract: Polymer electrolyte water electrolysis is considered as a pivotal technology for green hydrogen production. Iridium dioxide (IrO2) serves as the benchmark electrocatalyst for the anodic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) in these cells. However, the scarcity and cost of iridium drives efforts to find durable and cost-effective replacements or drastically reduce the iridium loading. While ruthenium dioxide (RuO2) offers comparable activity, its practical utility is impacted by its stability being inferior to IrO2. The presented computational study analyzes the metal-oxygen bond strengths in bulk IrO2 and RuO2 to provide insights into the electronic origins of their differing stabilities. Through a comparative analysis of the electronic structure of bulk rutile IrO2, RuO2, and selected MO2 systems, it is able to discriminate the covalent and ionic contributions to the metal-oxygen bond using crystal-orbital-derived electronic descriptors.

papers.title: Transducing quantum-spin-ice correlations into Weyl Fermi-arc transport at a synthetic Kondo lattice interface
papers.abstract: Quantum spin ice hosts collective excitations and quantum fluctuations that are largely electrically silent because the materials supporting them are insulating. Coupling this magnetic environment to surface-localized Weyl states offers a route to encode its correlations directly into Fermi-arc transport. Experimental access to this regime, however, has remained largely unexplored. Here, we realize a synthetic Kondo lattice interface between the Weyl semimetal $\mathrm{Eu_2Ir_2O_7}$ and the quantum-spin-ice candidate $\mathrm{Tb_2Ti_2O_7}$, and demonstrate that quantum-spin-ice correlations are imprinted on Weyl Fermi-arc transport. At ultra-low temperature, electronic transport evolves from a sixfold anisotropic response at low field into a twelvefold response over an intermediate field window, before entering a reentrant sixfold anisotropy at high field. No analogous twelvefold response occurs at the classical-spin-ice interface. The quantum--classical contrast shows that the same itinerant electronic channel acquires qualitatively different symmetry information when interacting with the quantum-fluctuating Tb moments, consistent with an interfacial coupling between the Weyl surface states and the transverse, multipolar degrees of freedom, in addition to the longitudinal, dipolar contribution. Our work establishes synthetic Kondo lattice interfaces as a route for transducing frustrated quantum magnetism with multipole correlations into distinct Weyl Fermi-arc transport responses.

papers.title: Accessing electronic entanglement via photo-assisted two-electron tomography
papers.abstract: Witnessing entanglement between electrons propagating in quantum circuits requires accessing their two-electron coherences, which encode the two-particle quantum correlations generated by Coulomb interactions. Yet, experimental reconstruction of two-electron coherence remains a major challenge. We introduce photo-assisted two-electron tomography, a quantum coherence reconstruction protocol from dc-currents and time-averaged current correlations, routinely measured in electron quantum optics experiments. Driving an energy filter with a small rf tone encodes off-diagonal coherences in the frequency domain into the dc-current response, enabling single-electron tomography without resorting to current-noise measurements. Extending it to two channels, current correlations after two photo-assisted filters reconstruct the two-electron Wigner distribution and isolate its irreducible two-body part. When applied to Coulomb-coupled quantum Hall edge channels, the protocol reveals interaction-induced energy entanglement. Signatures of this entanglement are visible through the violation of an entanglement witness based on Cauchy-Schwarz inequalities, as well as Wigner function negativities, which remain resolved above the thermal background for realistic device parameters. A generalized Franson geometry further extends the approach to intra-channel two-electron coherences. This opens a direct pathway to detect and characterize electronic entanglement in ballistic quantum circuits.

papers.title: A Universal Polybromide Melt Strategy for the Direct Conversion of Metals into Optoelectronic-Grade Bromide Perovskites
papers.abstract: Halide perovskite systems require specific metal oxidation states (M2+ or M+/M3+ pairs), limiting processing flexibility during traditional synthesis and posing stability challenges for multivalent metals like Sn, Cu, and Au. This work anchors a profound paradigm shift: a universal, single-step, organic-solvent free synthetic platform that directly converts stable elemental metal films into bromide perovskite and perovskite-related systems for a wide variety of (opto)electronic applications. The synthetic platform uses methylammonium polybromide melt (PBM) that reacts at room temperature with different elemental metals, including Pb, Sn, Au, and Cu, successfully transforming them into their respective Br-perovskite phases: MAPbBr3, MASnBr3, MA2Au2Br6, and MA2CuBr4. It is shown that the PBMs chemical activity can be tuned, and in situ X-ray diffraction captures in two cases transient intermediate phases during phase evolution. For Sn, which tends towards overoxidation to Sn4+ phase, changes in the PBMs composition coupled with a metallic Sn mediated comproportionation reaction allowed suppressing overoxidation, and formation of high quality MASnBr3 films under ambient conditions. Overall, oxidation and disproportionation potentials are found to be useful metrics for predicting M:PBM reaction outcomes. Industrially, this approach should be fully compatible with roll-to-roll infrastructure, providing a low-barrier pathway to scale next-generation optoelectronic technologies.

papers.title: Pressure-induced double-dome superconductivity in doped kagome metal Cs(V0.86Ta0.14)3Sb5 without charge density wave
papers.abstract: The vanadium-based kagome superconductor CsV$_3$Sb$_5$ exhibits an intricate interplay between charge density wave (CDW) and superconductivity (SC). Substituting Ta for V will suppress the CDW order and enhance superconductivity. Here, we report a high-pressure study up to 48 GPa on Ta-doped Cs(V$_{0.86}$Ta$_{0.14}$)$_3$Sb$_5$ with enhanced $T_\mathrm{c}$ around 5.29 K and without CDW order. At low pressures, unlike the characteristic $``$M-shaped" temperature-pressure phase diagram of the pristine CsV$_3$Sb$_5$, the Ta-doped compound exhibits a distinct non-monotonic evolution. Initially, $T_\mathrm{c}$ drops slightly from 5.29 K at ambient pressure to 4.90 K at 0.33 GPa, before increasing to a maximum of 5.70 K at 0.61 GPa. Upon further compression, $T_\mathrm{c}$ decreases continuously to 0.98 K at 12.3 GPa. At higher pressures, $T_\mathrm{c}$ rises again, reaching 4.46 K at 47.7 GPa. This evolution of $T_\mathrm{c}$ establishes two superconducting domes under pressure, which are similar to those in CsV$_3$Sb$_5$. Our results demonstrate that pressure-induced double-dome superconductivity is intrinsic to these V-based kagome superconductors, even in the absence of long-range CDW order.

papers.title: Measurement-induced enhancement of the $X$-parity lifetime in a Majorana tetron
papers.abstract: A recent experiment [arXiv:2507.08795] has reported measurements of the interwire $X$-parity lifetime in a Majorana tetron device via the quantum capacitance of an auxiliary readout dot. Motivated by these measurements, we theoretically study the interwire parity lifetime in a minimal model of the coupled dot-tetron system subject to electrostatic noise. We show that coupling to the measurement dot can itself strongly modify the parity dynamics by generating an energy splitting that shifts noise-induced transitions to finite frequency and thereby stabilizes the measured states against low-frequency fluctuations. For representative noise strengths motivated by disordered nanowire devices, we find $X$-parity switching lifetimes of order microseconds in the measurement configuration even when the corresponding bare-tetron coherence time is only tens of nanoseconds long. We analyze both the dispersive regime, where the dot can be integrated out and the dynamics reduces to an effective two-level system, and the near-resonant regime, where all four low-energy states participate. In the latter case, rapid transitions organize the spectrum into two long-lived manifolds that approximately correspond to sectors of the combined dot-tetron $X$-loop parity, yielding effective two-state switching despite the underlying multilevel structure. Our results show that measurement-induced stabilization can substantially enhance the observed $X$-parity switching lifetime, such that the lifetime measured under continuous readout can greatly exceed the intrinsic idle $T_2^*$ coherence time of the isolated Majorana tetron qubit.
